er.why: In the oncology literature 'ER' is the estrogen receptor (ER-positive/ER-negative disease): 98.7% of 451 declaring papers, with epiregulin declared zero times. The majority vote returns EREG (epiregulin).

psa.why: 'PSA' in cancer is prostate-specific antigen, KLK3: 528 of 528 declaring papers. Here the majority vote ALREADY returns KLK3, so the form stays blocklisted only because NPEPPS is a genuinely different gene. An earlier version of this note claimed the vote returned NPEPPS; that was asserted rather than measured, and was wrong.

cox-2.why: 'COX-2' in cancer pharmacology is prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2, the celecoxib target: 541 of 541 declaring papers, with the mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit II declared zero times. The majority vote returns the mitochondrial one.

p62.why: 'p62' in autophagy and redox signalling is sequestosome-1: 97.4% of 272 declaring papers. The majority vote returns NUP62, a nuclear pore protein.

p21.why: 'p21' as a cell-cycle inhibitor is CDKN1A: 89.6% of 336 declaring papers, the lowest share of the five because RAS p21 and a histone pseudogene are both real minority senses. The majority vote returns H3P16, the pseudogene.
